title: Company Store
logline: A retired miner's pension is paid entirely in company scrip that only works at a store that just declared bankruptcy.

roles.description: Gave their lungs and best years to the company; just wants to afford their medication.
Trapped managing a bankrupt store; feels intensely guilty about the voided pensions.
Sent to strip the company store of all remaining valuable assets.
A polished, utterly soulless administrative branch of the mining corp.
A decaying residential cylinder where the retired workforce is left to rot.
Once the center of commerce, now locked behind heavy corporate seals.
A massive conglomerate that views its workers as disposable machinery.

public_situation: The local branch of the {role:mining_corp} has filed for bankruptcy, voiding millions in employee pensions paid in company scrip.
private_truth: The bankruptcy is a restructuring trick. The corporation is intentionally voiding the scrip to clear their balance sheet before a massive merger.

beats.public_change: The company store officially locks its doors, posting a notice that all scrip is now invalid.

missions.reason: Needs a pilot to deliver their physical lockbox of lifetime scrip directly to a corporate regional office to plead for a cash buyout.
missions.private_fact: The miner only has a few weeks of lung medication left, and the scrip was supposed to pay for the refill.

beats.public_change: Corporate HQ publicly denies all buyout requests, citing bankruptcy laws.

missions.reason: The clerk quietly tells the pilot the scrip is entirely void, and begs them to use their own credits to buy black-market medicine and deliver it to the miner's habitat.
missions.private_fact: The clerk is risking prison by leaking the location of the uninventoried corporate medicine stash.

beats.public_change: The liquidators notice the missing medicine inventory and begin audits.

missions.reason: Hires the pilot to scan the store's cargo transponder logs from outside to prove the clerk embezzled the medicine.
missions.private_fact: If the liquidator can't find the medicine, they intend to charge the clerk with corporate treason.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot covers for the clerk.
resolutions.summary: The retired miner gets enough medicine to live comfortably for years. The liquidator writes the loss off as a clerical error.

consequences.public_summary: Someone bought a crate of meds out of pocket to save an old miner and scrubbed the ledger to protect the clerk.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot turns in the clerk's logs to the liquidator.
resolutions.summary: The corporation arrests the clerk and repossesses the medicine. The retired miner is left bankrupt and ruined.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot blackmails the liquidator using the logs.
resolutions.summary: The pilot profits off the corrupt liquidator. The corporation writes off the loss, and the miner barely survives on scraps.

loose_threads.detail: A shipping manifest stuck to the medicine crate lists an acquiring corporation's name, dated three months before the bankruptcy filing.
All the voided scrip carries a sequential serial block that was officially marked 'destroyed in transit' ten years ago.

radio_hooks: {role:mining_corp} announces record quarterly profits despite local branch bankruptcy.
Health officials warn of critical medication shortages following company store closures.

voice_direction.retired_miner: Slow, halting rhythm. Pauses frequently. Uses very short words.
voice_direction.company_store_clerk: Frantic, fast pace. Constantly interrupts themselves with apologies.
voice_direction.corporate_liquidator: Bored, cold pitch. Pronounces every syllable perfectly.
